sessions.task:
You are a read-only scout. Work ONLY inside this project. Do not modify files, do not network.

GOAL: From experiment-data/agnews-64k.txt, find ALL instances associated with user ID 91245, classify each unlabeled news instance into one of: World, Business, Sci/Tech, Sports, and determine which label among {World, Business, Sci/Tech} is most common for that user (Sports may appear but the question asks among those three).

DATA FORMAT: Lines look like:
Date: ... || User: <id> || Instance: <headline and lead>

TASKS:
1. Extract every line where User is exactly 91245.
2. For each instance, classify the topic carefully based on the full text. Categories:
   - World: international news, politics, war, diplomacy, disasters abroad, elections outside pure business
   - Business: markets, companies, economy, oil prices as market news, earnings, trade, corporate
   - Sci/Tech: technology, science, software, internet, space, research, gadgets
   - Sports: athletic competitions, teams, players, leagues
3. Count labels for user 91245 only.
4. Report the most common among World, Business, Sci/Tech.

REQUIRED EVIDENCE FORMAT in your final report:
- total_instances_for_user
- per-instance list: line_number | brief_headline | label | 1-sentence justification
- label_counts: {World: n, Business: n, Sci/Tech: n, Sports: n}
- most_common_among_asked: one of World|Business|Sci/Tech
- tie-break note if any

Do NOT guess labels without reading the text. Be exact. Acceptance: complete enumeration of all user 91245 rows with classifications and counts.
